about: The epistola of the formulary “13th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. He does not say: And to seeds, as referring to many, but as referring to one: And to your seed, who is Christ. Now this I say: the law, which came into being four hundred and thirty years afterward, does not so annul the testament confirmed by God as to cancel the promise. For if the inheritance comes from the law, then it no longer comes from the promise. But to Abraham God granted it by promise. What, then, is the law? It was laid down because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom He had made the promise, ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator. Now a mediator is not of one; God, however, is one. So is the law against the promises of God? Far from it. For if there had been given a law able to give life, justice would indeed come from the law. But Scripture has confined all things under sin, so that the promise might be granted, from the faith of Jesus Christ, to those who believe.
